analysis.investment_thesis: LXCHEM fails the Magic Formula on both dimensions: Earnings Yield of ~6.9% (EBIT ₹286 Cr / EV ~₹4,155 Cr) is below my 12% minimum, and ROCE of 8.56% is less than half the 20% threshold I require. With net profit declining from ₹256 Cr (FY22) to ₹114 Cr (FY25) while the stock trades at 49.5x trailing earnings, this is a deteriorating business dressed up in an expensive valuation.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 12.3% over 9 years shows the acetyl/specialty chemical franchise has durable demand
Low D/E of 0.17 keeps financial risk manageable despite rising borrowings in FY25
High promoter holding of 69.4% aligns management with long-term outcomes
key_risks: Profitability in freefall: net profit down 55% from ₹256 Cr (FY22) peak to ₹114 Cr (FY25), operating margin only 4.1%
FCF deeply negative at -₹286 Cr in FY25 due to ₹394 Cr capex; CWIP of ₹462 Cr signals capex cycle still not complete
Valuation at 49.5x trailing P/E with declining earnings is speculative — Magic Formula never buys earnings hope at this yield
red_flags: Earnings yield of ~6.9% fails Magic Formula minimum of 12% — not cheap enough to compensate for poor ROIC
ROCE 8.56% and ROE 5.93% are both well below cost of capital — capital allocation is value-destructive at these return levels
Borrowings nearly tripled from ₹143 Cr (FY24) to ₹334 Cr (FY25) despite ongoing equity on balance sheet — concerning capital discipline
Net profit declining 4 consecutive years post-FY22 super-cycle peak; not a temporary dip
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on LXCHEM: EV = Market Cap (₹3,939 Cr) + Net Debt (₹258 - ₹42 Cr = ₹216 Cr) = ~₹4,155 Cr. Earnings Yield = EBIT ₹286 Cr / EV ₹4,155 Cr = 6.9% — barely above my hard floor of 6%, nowhere near the 12%+ that makes a stock attractive. ROCE of 8.56% tells the same story on the quality side — this business earns well below its cost of capital. When both legs of the Magic Formula are broken, I walk away.

The deeper issue is what happened post-FY22: the commodity cycle inflated EBIT to ₹371 Cr and net profit to ₹256 Cr, and the market re-rated the stock as a high-quality compounder. But FY23-25 has revealed mean reversion — margins compressed back to 4.1% operating, net profit has halved, and the company is now spending aggressively on capex (₹394 Cr in FY25 alone, CWIP of ₹462 Cr) funded partly by debt. The forward P/E of 28x implies analysts expect a sharp earnings recovery from capex payoff, but I don't pay for hope — I pay for proven, high ROIC businesses at cheap prices. LXCHEM offers neither right now.
